root_cause.text: ksmbd's smb_check_perm_dacl() performed incomplete ACE length validation, accepting ACEs whose declared size was smaller than the smb_ace fields later accessed (access_req and sid/sub_auth), leading to out-of-bounds reads while walking DACLs.
root_cause.evidence: The commit states both ACE-walk loops only checked remaining buffer size and allowed crafted `ace->size == 4` to pass, after which `le32_to_cpu(ace->access_req)` and `compare_sids(&sid, &ace->sid)` read past the ACE; the patch fixes this by requiring `ace_size >= offsetof(struct smb_ace, sid) + CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE` and rejecting `sid.num_subauth > SID_MAX_SUB_AUTHORITIES`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add stricter bounds validation for SMB ACE entries so malformed DACL data with incomplete SID content is rejected safely.
intent_record.what: The loop's DACL ACE validation was changed from a single size check `offsetof(struct smb_ace, access_req) > aces_size` to a check that the remaining buffer can hold the ACE up to its SID plus at least `CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE`, and the ACE size validation was expanded from only `ace_size > aces_size` to also reject ACEs smaller than `offsetof(struct smb_ace, sid) + CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes ACE parsing reject truncated or undersized ACE entries before reading their fields, preventing the code from processing malformed ACL data that does not contain a minimally valid SID structure and avoiding potential out-of-bounds access or incorrect permission evaluation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add stricter bounds and SID validation when parsing DACL ACEs to safely reject malformed ACL entries.
intent_record.what: The loop that parses DACL ACE entries in smb_check_perm_dacl() was modified to strengthen ACE validation: the initial size check was changed from comparing offsetof(struct smb_ace, access_req) against aces_size to checking that the remaining bytes can at least hold offsetof(struct smb_ace, sid) plus CIFS_SID_BASE_SIZE; the ace_size validation was expanded to reject ACEs whose size is either larger than the remaining buffer or smaller than the minimum size needed for the SID base fields; and a new check was added to break if ace->sid.num_subauth exceeds SID_MAX_SUB_AUTHORITIES.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the function from processing malformed or truncated ACE records and from trusting invalid SID subauthority counts while walking the DACL. It reduces the risk of out-of-bounds reads or parsing corrupt ACL data by stopping iteration when an ACE is too short, oversized, or contains an invalid SID layout.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it contains the ACE-walking logic and the length checks before later field accesses. The vulnerable construct is present: in both ACE iteration loops, the code only checks `if (offsetof(struct smb_ace, access_req) > aces_size) break;` (lines 1240-1241 and 1261-1262) and then reads `ace->size` and `ace->access_req` (`ace_size = le16_to_cpu(ace->size);` at 1242/1263, `granted |= le32_to_cpu(ace->access_req);` at 1246, and later `le32_to_cpu(ace->access_req)` at 1283, 1331, 1335, 1343). This validates only that enough bytes remain up to `access_req`, not that the declared ACE length `ace_size` is at least large enough to contain all fields subsequently accessed. The code also accesses `ace->sid` in `compare_sids(&sid, &ace->sid)` and `compare_sids(&sid_unix_NFS_mode, &ace->sid)` (1268-1269) and `compare_sids(&sid_everyone, &ace->sid)` (1273) without ensuring `ace_size` covers the SID/sub_auth area. The check `if (ace_size > aces_size) break;` only ensures the ACE does not extend past the buffer, but does not reject malformed ACEs whose own declared size is too small for `access_req`/`sid`. Therefore the incomplete ACE length validation described in the root cause exists here. Since there is no minimum-size validation such as rejecting `ace_size < offsetofend(...)` or validating SID length before these accesses, the fix is not present.
